sequence_description: I1 attack: JWKS key-rotation/kid-confusion — after switching the mount trust anchor to a different public key set, a JWT signed by the OLD key but carrying a 'kid' that matches a key in the NEW trust set must be rejected (no semantic proof confusion across trust anchors). Includes control login before and after config change.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT trust-anchor rotation did not invalidate tokens signed by the old key: after reconfiguring JWT validation, an attacker JWT with an old signature was still accepted (kid-confusion/rotation bypass).

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT trust-anchor rotation did not invalidate tokens signed by the old key: after reconfiguring JWT validation, an attacker JWT with an old signature was still accepted (kid-confusion/rotation bypass).

sequence_description: Replay the same signed JWT after revoking the first session token; revocation should not be bypassable by reusing the same JWT within its validity window.
description: [LLM-Judge] Revoked JWT-auth session appears to remain usable because the replay login returned the exact same Vault session token/accessor after revocation (suggesting revocation did not take effect or token was re-minted deterministically).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Revoked JWT-auth session appears to remain usable because the replay login returned the exact same Vault session token/accessor after revocation (suggesting revocation did not take effect or token was re-minted deterministically).

sequence_description: Attack I2 by submitting a JWT with iat far in the future (time-travel token). Control login uses a valid token. Role is configured with clock_skew_leeway=0 (sentinel default 60s) to probe whether Vault incorrectly accepts a token with iat far beyond allowable skew.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT with iat far in the future was accepted, suggesting missing/ineffective iat freshness enforcement (potential time-skew bypass depending on expected validation semantics).

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT with iat far in the future was accepted, suggesting missing/ineffective iat freshness enforcement (potential time-skew bypass depending on expected validation semantics).

sequence_description: JWT trust-anchor rotation coherence: login succeeds with key-A, then admin rotates jwt_validation_pubkeys to key-B; re-login with same key-A-signed JWT should be rejected (no stale cache / no cross-config acceptance).
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT signing-key rotation did not invalidate subsequent login (possible stale JWKS/public-key cache or mis-rotation), as a post-rotation JWT login still succeeded.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT signing-key rotation did not invalidate subsequent login (possible stale JWKS/public-key cache or mis-rotation), as a post-rotation JWT login still succeeded.
